title: Home
metaTitle: Oil & Gas Royalty Buyer - Sell Your Royalty Interest
metaDescription: A direct buyer for oil and gas royalty and mineral interests, run by a former operations engineer who reads your statement before making an offer.
heroLead: Your royalty check is the most honest document you own about what your minerals are worth. We start there, not with a guess.
intro: We buy producing and non-producing oil and gas royalty and mineral interests directly from owners - no broker commission, no obligation to accept what we offer. What sets our review apart is where we start: your actual royalty statements, read the way an operations engineer reads them, not a form letter built off a county average.

Whether you're holding a fractional interest inherited three generations back or a straightforward royalty on a well you've watched produce for years, we'll walk through what your statements actually show before we ever put a number in front of you.

sections.heading: What we actually look at
paragraphs: Send us your recent statements, or just a legal description and county if that's all you have, and we'll read the decimal interest, the production trend, and the deduction lines the way we used to on the operating side - because that's genuinely where the real information lives, not in a summary someone else wrote for you.

A well six months in with a shallow decline reads very differently from a stripper well near the end of its life, even if this month's check looks similar. That distinction is the difference between a fair offer and a lazy one, and it's the first thing we work out.

sections.heading: How the process runs
paragraphs: Send your information - statements, deed, or whatever paperwork you have, even if it's incomplete. We review your decimal interest, production history, and any nearby drilling activity, and put together a written offer, typically within a few business days depending on how much documentation is available. You review it with no obligation to accept, and take as long as you reasonably need. If you accept, we handle the purchase agreement and title work, and funds are disbursed once the deed is signed and recorded.

We'll tell you plainly if title issues - an unresolved heirship, a missing signature - need to be cleared before closing, and we'll explain what that involves rather than leaving you to figure it out.

sections.heading: Reading the check honestly
paragraphs: Deductions, decline, and the decimal interest line confuse most owners, and most buyers have no interest in explaining any of it, because a confused seller is easier to lowball. We built a full guide to reading your royalty statement line by line, and we'll walk you through your specific stub directly if you'd rather ask a person than read an article.

We'll also tell you honestly when we think holding makes more sense than selling - a well early in its life with strong nearby activity is sometimes worth more to you as a royalty owner than as a lump sum today, and we'd rather say that than push a deal that doesn't serve you.

sections.heading: Producing, non-producing, whole or fractional
paragraphs: We evaluate producing royalty interests, non-producing minerals, overriding royalty interests, and net profits interests, whether you own the whole tract or a small fraction split among heirs. Small fractional interests are often the ones owners assume aren't worth pursuing - they're frequently worth more attention than owners expect, and the administrative hassle of tracking a tiny check across a large family is itself a reason some owners choose to sell.

sections.heading: Coverage across active basins
paragraphs: We evaluate interests across the major producing basins and plays - the Permian, the Bakken, the Eagle Ford, Appalachian gas country, the Anadarko and Ark-La-Tex, and other established production areas. Activity and value differ meaningfully basin to basin and even county to county within a basin, which is exactly why we review your specific production data rather than applying a single regional number to every owner who contacts us.

faqs.question: How fast can you get an offer?
faqs.answer: Typically within a few business days once we have your statements or a usable legal description, though incomplete paperwork can add time while we pull county records. We'll give you a realistic estimate once we see what you have.

faqs.question: What documents do you need to make an offer?
faqs.answer: Recent royalty statements are the most useful, along with a deed or legal description if you have one. We can often start with less - even just a county and rough description - and fill gaps from public records.

faqs.question: Is there any cost or obligation to get an offer?
faqs.answer: No. Getting an offer is free and carries no obligation to sell. You're free to compare it against other offers or simply decide to keep your interest.

faqs.question: What if you only own a fraction of an interest?
faqs.answer: We regularly buy fractional and inherited interests, including small shares split among several heirs. Your exact decimal interest is what we evaluate, not an assumption about whether a small share is worth pursuing.

faqs.question: Do you deduct anything from the offer amount?
faqs.answer: We're direct buyers, not brokers, so there's no commission taken from your proceeds. Closing costs and title work are handled as part of the transaction terms, which we'll spell out clearly in the purchase agreement before you sign anything.
